title: Chat Relay Recipe
description: Describes how to drive one chat UI's DOM well enough to relay HUMAN-MCP CALL/RESULT blocks through it automatically. This is the authoritative field-level reference - also see docs/recipe-authoring.md in this package for the narrative guide (how to explore a page, pick a completion strategy, common pitfalls) that this schema's descriptions summarize.

schemaVersion.description: Must be exactly 1. The only version this extension understands - do not guess at a different number.

id.description: Stable slug, e.g. "deepseek". This is the storage primary key, NOT hostname - so two recipes may target the same hostname (e.g. an old vs. new UI variant) without colliding. Must be unique among already-uploaded recipes.

hostname.description: Exact location.hostname of the chat page, e.g. "chat.deepseek.com" - no scheme, path, or port. Matched exactly, not as a pattern.

displayName.description: Optional human-readable label shown in the extension popup, e.g. "DeepSeek". Defaults to hostname if omitted.

selector.description: CSS selector for the chat's message-input element (a <textarea> or contenteditable element). Prefer a stable attribute (placeholder text, aria-label) over a hashed/generated CSS-module class name, which can change on any site redeploy.

setVia.description: How to set the input's text so the site's own framework (React, etc.) notices the change. "native-value-setter" is for a real <textarea>/<input> whose value is controlled by a JS framework - plain `el.value = text` is silently ignored by React-controlled inputs, so this strategy sets the value via the native property setter (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype,'value').set) and then dispatches a bubbling 'input' event, which IS what React listens for. "contenteditable-text" is for a contenteditable div (not yet implemented as of schemaVersion 1 - a recipe requesting it will fail loudly at runtime, not silently misbehave; only declare it if you've confirmed a future version implements it).

selector.description: CSS selector for the send/submit button. Must be clickable via el.click() once the input has text (some sites disable this button while the input is empty - that's fine, the recipe sets the input value first). No "press Enter instead" fallback exists - if the site truly requires a click, this selector must resolve to it.

containerSelector.description: CSS selector matching each assistant reply's final-answer text container. IMPORTANT: many chat UIs render a separate "thinking"/reasoning trace alongside the actual answer (e.g. a sibling element with different styling/class) - this selector must match ONLY the final answer text, never the reasoning trace, or the relay will try to parse HUMAN-MCP CALL sentinels out of scratchpad text that was never meant to contain them. Verify this by triggering a reply that visibly shows a reasoning/thinking section and confirming the selector's matched text excludes it.

pick.description: Which match of containerSelector to read. Only "last" is implemented (reads the most recent reply). "nth" is reserved for a future version - do not use it, a recipe with pick:"nth" is rejected at validation time.

completion.description: How to detect that the assistant has finished streaming its reply, before reading it. Pick ONE strategy based on what's actually observable on the page - see docs/recipe-authoring.md for how to choose.

observe.description: CSS selector to watch for DOM mutations (text/children changing) - typically the same as, or an ancestor of, reply.containerSelector's last match. Falls back to document.body if the selector currently matches nothing (e.g. before any reply exists yet).

idleMs.description: Resolve once this many milliseconds pass with no further mutations on the observed node. Use this strategy when there's no reliable stop-button or disabled-state signal, only visibly-streaming text. Pick idleMs generously (3000ms+ recommended) - a reasoning model's thinking pauses between sentences can easily exceed a short idle threshold, causing a truncated mid-stream reply to be read before the actual answer/call block is written.

maxWaitMs.description: Hard timeout (ms, max 10 minutes) - if no completion signal fires before this, the wait fails with a timeout error rather than hanging forever.

watchSelector.description: CSS selector for a "stop generating"/regenerate-style button that appears while streaming and disappears (or is replaced by a different button) once done. Completion is: selector seen present, then subsequently absent. Prefer this strategy when such a button exists - it's the most reliable signal, since it's the same signal the site's own UI relies on.

CSS selector for an element (often the same as submit.selector) whose `disabled` property flips to true while streaming and back to false once done. Completion is: seen disabled, then subsequently re-enabled. Use this when the submit button itself is disabled during generation and no separate stop button exists.

startSentinel.description: Defaults to "HUMAN-MCP CALL" if omitted - leave unset unless you have a specific reason to deviate from the standard human-mcp-relay protocol.

endSentinel.description: Defaults to "HUMAN-MCP END" if omitted - leave unset unless you have a specific reason to deviate from the standard human-mcp-relay protocol.
